riskReasons: The same cultivar appears under diacritic, non-diacritic, hyphenated, spaced and joined romanised forms.
RHS and Missouri Botanical Garden support the same spring-red, compact Acer palmatum identity, but summer white speckling is stated by RHS and not repeated by Missouri Botanical Garden.
Separate accepted cultivars ‘Deshōjō’ and ‘Deshōjō-nishiki’ create a near-name risk that requires explicit non-synonym treatment.

duplicateCheck.notes: Compared with RC-001–RC-010 and all other approved Catalogue assignments. Shin-deshōjō, Shin-deshojo and Shindeshojo are orthographic forms of this one identity, not separate cultivars. RHS separately accepts ‘Deshōjō’ and ‘Deshōjō-nishiki’; neither is treated as a synonym. C0 resolves as unique with targeted romanisation review complete.

identityNotes: The public working form is ‘Shin-deshōjō’, following the current RHS accepted heading and preserving the macrons and hyphen. Non-diacritic ‘Shin-deshojo’, joined ‘Shindeshojo’ and spaced label forms are search variants for the same cultivar. ‘Deshōjō’ and ‘Deshōjō-nishiki’ remain separate accepted cultivars.

content.summary: A compact, bushy Japanese maple prized for an intense crimson-red spring flush that gradually shifts through reddish green to green in summer and returns to red and orange tones in autumn.
content.habit: Compact, slow-growing, upright-rounded to bushy deciduous shrub or small tree. Published institutional ranges place it broadly around 1.5–3 m high and wide over time.
content.leafForm: Small palmate leaves, commonly five to seven lobed, with ovate pointed lobes and serrated margins. The principal diagnostic interest is the spring colour sequence rather than an unusual leaf division.

seasonal.spring: Leaves emerge bright crimson to showy red and may retain strong red colour for roughly a month, depending on climate and exposure.
seasonal.summer: Foliage fades through reddish green to green. RHS additionally reports white speckling, a feature not repeated in the Missouri Botanical Garden account and therefore retained as source-specific.
seasonal.autumn: Leaves turn reddish orange to mixed red and orange shades.

size.qualifier: RHS gives 1.5–2.5 m high and wide over 10–20 years; Missouri Botanical Garden gives 5–7 ft commonly and up to about 10 ft over time. Preserve both as contextual ranges.

content.cultivation: Grow in moist but well-drained, preferably slightly acidic soil in a sheltered position. Partial shade helps preserve leaf quality and colour; full sun may be tolerated with reliable moisture. Protect early foliage from drying winds, scorch and late spring frost.
content.diagnostic: The strongest comparison feature is the sustained vivid crimson spring flush on a compact bushy plant. Do not create separate identities from Shin-deshojo or Shindeshojo labels, and do not merge the cultivar with separately accepted ‘Deshōjō’ or ‘Deshōjō-nishiki’.
content.confidence: High confidence that the principal romanised forms refer to one accepted Acer palmatum cultivar and in the broad spring-to-summer colour sequence. Moderate confidence in white summer speckling and mature size because the institutional descriptions differ.
content.unresolvedIssue: The lean review did not locate a primary Japanese naming or introduction record. The frequency and diagnostic value of RHS-reported white summer speckling remain unresolved and must not be treated as mandatory for authentication.
